sections.html:
Dubois County is in southwest Indiana, and Jasper is both the county seat and the largest city. The county covers 435.33 square miles, of which 427.27 are land and 8.06 are water.

It borders Martin, Orange, Crawford, Perry, Spencer, Warrick, Pike and Daviess counties. Patoka Lake lies along the eastern border with Crawford and Orange counties and hosts national bass fishing tournaments. Part of Hoosier National Forest is inside the county. Jasper stands along the Patoka River at 466 feet above sea level.

Weather is a practical issue for homes here. Average temperatures in Jasper run from about 20 degrees Fahrenheit in January to 86 in July, so heating and cooling systems both get used.

sections.h2: What is the history of Dubois County?
sections.html:
Dubois County was formed on December 20, 1818, from parts of Orange, Pike and Perry counties. It was named for Toussaint Dubois, a French-born veteran of the Revolutionary War, the Battle of Tippecanoe and the War of 1812.

Portersville was the original county seat, and the seat moved to Jasper in 1830. Jasper was founded in 1818 and platted in 1830, incorporated as a town in 1866 and as a city in 1915. Milk sickness reportedly killed as many as half of the county's residents in 1818.

A smaller local story: Dubois County switched to Central Time in 2006 and returned to Eastern Time in 2007, and both changes were controversial.

sections.h2: What does the Dubois County economy look like?
sections.html:
Jasper calls itself the Wood Capital of the World, and manufacturing is the county's largest employment sector, followed by retail and health care. Furniture and cabinet makers in Jasper include Jasper Group, Kimball International and MasterBrand Cabinets.

Other employers named include Jasper Engines and Transmissions and the Southern Indiana Education Center. The city also hosts Vincennes University's Jasper Campus. Public schools in Jasper include Jasper High School, Jasper Middle School, Ireland Elementary and Jasper Elementary, and the Holy Trinity Catholic School campuses serve private families.

The county is part of the Jasper Micropolitan Statistical Area, which is now made up of Dubois County alone, since Pike County was removed in 2023. Huntingburg, Ferdinand and the community of Dubois are other named places in the county.

Whatever the employer, anyone selling a house here still needs a clear tax record before closing.

sections.h2: How many people live in Dubois County?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted 43,637 people in Dubois County, up from 41,889 in 2010, and the 2025 estimate is 44,016. The median age is 41.2, and the county has 17,412 households. About 9.5% of residents are Hispanic or Latino, and about 52.4% live in urban areas.

Jasper had 16,703 residents in 2020, up from 15,038 in 2010 and 12,100 in 2000, which makes it the 48th largest city in Indiana. It lies within Bainbridge, Boone and Madison townships, and 98.2% of its residents live in urban areas. The county votes in Indiana's 8th congressional district.

The county added about 1,750 residents over the decade.

sections.h2: Who handles Dubois County property assessment?
sections.html:
The Dubois County Assessor is Angela C. Giesler, and the office is at One Courthouse Square, Jasper, IN 47546. The phone number is 812-481-7010, the email is assessor@duboiscountyin.org, and hours are Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

The assessor's page lists these recurring dates:

  • January 1: the assessment date each year
  • April 1: Form 136 property tax exemption applications are due
  • May 15: business personal property returns are due, moving to the next business day if it falls on a weekend
  • December 31: affidavits for destroyed or removed property are due

The office also requires a Notice of Assessment Registration when a project needs no building permit, with a $100 civil penalty for failure to file. If you built or removed a structure, the assessor needs to know before a buyer's review.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Dubois County assessment?
sections.html:
You appeal a Dubois County assessment with Form 130, which the assessor's site links under "Appeal an assessment." The county page does not state the deadline, so use the state rule: June 15 of the year the notice or tax bill is mailed.

One petition covers one parcel. After the assessor's informal meeting, the Property Tax Assessment Board of Appeals holds a hearing within 180 days of filing, with notice mailed at least 30 days ahead. A $50 penalty may apply if you miss the hearing with no valid continuance. Disputes go on to the Indiana Board of Tax Review through Form 131.

sections.h2: How does a Dubois County tax sale work?
sections.html:
The Dubois County tax sale usually happens in September or October for parcels with a balance due from the spring of the prior year or earlier. In mid-July, the Auditor's office usually mails a certified letter to each listed owner.

Owners can pay up to the time of the sale. Contact the Treasurer at One Courthouse Square, Jasper, at 812-481-7080 or treasurer@duboiscountyin.org, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

sections.h2: When are Dubois County property taxes due, and what are the penalties?
sections.html:
Indiana sets two installment dates, May 10 and November 10, and the state calendar listed May 11 and November 10 for 2026. We did not find Dubois County's own due-date notice on an official page, so confirm with the Treasurer.

The late penalty is 5% if you pay within 30 days of the due date and have no earlier delinquency, and 10% otherwise. Later installments can bring extra 10% penalties. Under the statute we reviewed, the standard homestead deduction is 60% of assessed value up to $48,000 for assessment dates after 2022, filed by January 5, and it was amended effective January 1, 2025.

sections.h2: What do Dubois County sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Sellers in Dubois County commonly deal with inherited homes, outdated houses and unpaid tax. Before closing, Indiana requires a sales disclosure form that the assessor reviews before the deed reaches the auditor, one form per parcel.

  • Ask the Treasurer for the current balance and any tax sale charges.
  • Check the assessor's records for additions or removed structures.
  • Collect estate documents and prior tax bills.
  • Decide whether to repair or sell as is.

A cash purchase can close quickly, with taxes settled at the title company from your proceeds.

faqs.q: Where is the Dubois County Assessor's office?
faqs.a: The Assessor is at One Courthouse Square, Jasper, IN 47546. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., and the phone is 812-481-7010.

faqs.q: When does the Dubois County tax sale happen?
faqs.a: The county usually holds its tax sale in September or October. A certified letter normally goes to listed owners in mid-July, and owners can pay up to the time of the sale.

faqs.q: How long do I have to redeem Dubois County property after a tax sale?
faqs.a: The prior owner has one year to redeem the tax certificate. After that the Auditor's office gives a deed to the certificate holder.

faqs.q: What is the Dubois County tax sale charge?
faqs.a: A $130.00 charge is added to each parcel's amount due once it is listed for tax sale.

faqs.q: When are Dubois County exemption applications due?
faqs.a: Form 136 property tax exemption applications are due April 1, according to the Assessor's page.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Dubois County house with back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance and penalties are paid from your proceeds at closing, and selling before the sale date avoids the added tax sale charge.
